brief: September CPI surprised to the upside: headline rose 0.65% m/m (3.7% y/y) and core rose 0.33% m/m (2.6% y/y), both above consensus for a second straight month, accelerating 25bps and 4bps respectively from August. Energy drove most of the headline gain, with gasoline up roughly 9.5% m/m on Middle East-related supply concerns contributing nearly 40bps of the 65bps rise, and higher oil and jet fuel costs also lifting airfares 1.2% m/m. Core goods and core services reaccelerated too: information technology pricing jumped on AI-related demand and supply constraints, core goods rose 0.25% m/m versus a 0.07% three-month average, and core services rose 0.37% m/m on travel and firmer housing costs. That broad-based firmness, plus core PCE still near 3% and resilient growth (1H near 2.5% annualized, 3Q tracking 3%), leads UBS to add a third Fed hike: now September and December 2026 plus March 2027, followed by a first cut in late 2027, a path it still calls more dovish than market pricing of roughly five total hikes.
